title: Stubbed route scratch notebook: eu-west-1 regional handoff
content:
Purpose:
Quick scratchpad for the eu-west-1 handoff that started ~2026-03-08T21:12Z. Personal notes for reproductions, commands tried, raw error snippets, and prioritized hypotheses. This is messy by design — triage breadcrumbs for follow-up.

1) What I saw (high level):
- Spike in 5xxs from hosted API customers targeting eu-west-1 between 2026-03-08T21:10Z and 21:40Z.
- Many requests observed to complete with a 504 gateway timeout at the edge, while upstream logs show GRPC STREAM RESET/DEADLINE_EXCEEDED at the serving-router -> region-proxy hop.
- Automatic fallback policy routed a handful of requests to us-east-1 model-variants which caused increased cross-region p99 latency for two tenants.

2) Timeline (quick):
- 21:09: internal alert: p95 latency (eu-west-1) > 1.8s
- 21:12: first 5xx surge; edge shows 503 -> fallback executed
- 21:15: short SRE mitigation: bumped route weight away from failing nodes (manual)
- 21:23: another cluster of resets, observed a correlation with large-batch inference requests (seq_len ~ 4096)
- 21:40: incident quieted after autoscaler added capacity + temporary routing policy change

3) Repro (local / quick):
- Tried to reproduce locally against a small repro cluster (devnet) with similar config and a heavy batched request pattern:
  - ./redwoodctl cluster create --name repro-eu --region eu-west-1 --size small
  - docker-compose run client sh -c 'ab -n 200 -c 4 -p ./big-payload.json -T application/json http://repro-eu.local/v1/generate'
  - Observed timeouts when batch size > 32 tokens/step and when KV cache miss rate spiked

4) Commands & snippets I ran (raw):
- redwoodctl route inspect eu-west-1 --route default --verbose\  (output: route policy shows fallback: allow->region-priority: [eu-west-1, us-east-1], ttl=60s)
- redwoodctl logs --since 2026-03-08T21:00Z --component region-proxy --region eu-west-1 | rg "STREAM_RESET|DEADLINE_EXCEEDED" -n
- kubectl -n serving logs router-pod-7fd8 --since=30m | tail -n 150
- tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/eu-west-handovers.pcap 'tcp port 443'

Example raw lines captured from router logs:
[2026-03-08T21:12:07Z] router-7fd8 INFO request-id=abc123 path=/v1/generate decision=fallback target=us-east-1 reason=cluster_capacity_low
[2026-03-08T21:12:09Z] proxy-4a2c WARN upstream=worker-22 error=GRPC: "stream terminated by RST_STREAM" code=GRPC_STREAM_RESET

Edge curl trace for a single failed request:
* Connected to api.redwood.local (10.4.2.8) port 443 (#0)
> POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.local
> Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
> Content-Type: application/json
> Content-Length: 38192
< HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
< Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2026 21:12:17 GMT
< Content-Type: application/json
< x-redwood-request-id: abc123
{"error":"upstream deadline exceeded"}

5) Observations & correlations:
- The first wave correlates with a tenant who sent 6 concurrent long-seq requests (seq_len ~ 4096) — these requests increased kernel-level context switches and elevated IO wait on the GPU nodes (per metrics).
- GRPC stream resets appear primarily on the proxy <-> worker link, not on the edge -> proxy link. Implication: transport between region-proxy and model-worker had issues (OOM, long gc, or network flaps).
- KV cache miss spikes preceded some of the timeouts; could be a cascading cost: miss -> larger compute -> slower response -> router hits capacity threshold -> fallback triggers -> cross-region tail latency increases.

6) Hypotheses (ranked):
A) (High) Worker-level overload caused GRPC resets. Large batches + cold KV cache -> longer compute -> exceeded GRPC stream deadlines leading proxy to close stream (RST). Evidence: worker metrics show GPU util ~98%, GPU mem pressure, and RT > usual.
B) (Med) Region-proxy misconfiguration: per-connection keepalive/timeout settings too aggressive for long-running model execs. Evidence: resets timed out at ~16s, matching a default keepalive/window.
C) (Low) Control-plane route update race: simultaneous autoscaler adds + manual weight change produced ephemeral misrouting to nodes not fully initialized. Evidence: some fallback lines reference target=us-east-1 while region node count showed +0 shortly before update.
D) (Exploratory) Kernel-level TCP conn tracking bug when many large payloads arrive (observed a handful of TCP retransmits in tcpdump).

7) Quick mitigations executed during incident:
- Temporarily raised region-proxy GRPC deadline from 20s -> 45s for eu-west-1 (manual)
- Increased serving-pool capacity by 2 mid-tier GPUs (autoscaler + manual override)
- Added per-tenant request-size throttling for heuristics to prevent multi-4096 concurrent requests (temporary rule)

8) Repro notes (what failed to reproduce fully):
- Could not reproduce exact GRPC RST pattern on devnet without throttling GPU memory and forcing KV eviction. When I artificially limited GPU memory in the worker container (cgroups), the proxy resets showed up similarly — this strengthens overloaded worker hypothesis.

9) Next steps (short):
- [Evan] collect detailed worker-side GDB traces for the busiest pod that had resets (JIRA INF-5123)
- [Diego] make a small test that simulates large-batch KV miss pattern and run it against canary pool with verbose tracing
- [Maya] propose a permanent change: increase region-proxy deadline for model-exec-heavy routes OR implement adaptive deadline tied to expected token count per request
- Add a one-click rollback to previous routing-policy when autoscaler changes coincide with manual weight edits (reduce race surface)

10) Long-term ideas:
- Adaptive timeouts: derive soft deadlines from historical token throughput for a (model, seq_len) pair.
- Smarter fallback trigger: prefer local degraded nodes with soft-capacity over immediate cross-region fallback if predicted cross-region latency > threshold.
- Harden GRPC keepalive knobs and add explicit backpressure signal from worker to proxy instead of stream RST (explicit 429-style preflight).

11) Open questions / unknowns:
- Why did KV miss rate spike? Was there an eviction TTL miscalculation? (need to grep cache-evict logs)
- Did the autoscaler scale up sufficiently quickly? Check HPA and controller-manager events for gaps.
- Are there NIC-level errors on the worker hosts during the event window? (ask infra team for host-level logs)

12) Raw grep pointers (useful commands next time):
- rg "request-id=abc123" -n /var/log/redwood/* --hidden
- redwoodctl obs tail --component worker --region eu-west-1 --since 30m | rg "evict|kv-cache|OOM|cuda" -n
- sudo journalctl -u kubelet --since "2026-03-08 21:00" | rg "NodeNotReady|Eviction"

13) TODO (Taylor):
- Turn this scratchpad into a short incident writeup once we confirm root cause.
- Draft an ops-safe change for region-proxy default deadlines and get review from @platform-eng.

----
Personal notes: I kept the manual change small because cascading fallbacks to us-east increased costs and customer p99. If the hypothesis about worker overload holds, longer-term solution likely spans serving-runtime (adaptive deadlines), scheduler (prefer warm nodes for long sequences), and optimize cache TTL behavior.

End of scratch notes.
